question: The molecular formula, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}$, has five (5) structural isomers, name them. (5 marks)
Give the names of the first three members of the cycloalkane series. (3 marks)
Name two (2) general type of reactions of cycloalkanes. (2 marks)

Classify the following compounds as primary, secondary or tertiary haloalkanes. (5 marks)
(a) 2-iodopropane
(b) 2-chloro-2-methylpropane
(c) 1-chloro-2-methylpropane
(d) 3-bromopentane
(e) 1-bromobutane

Classify the following compounds as primary, secondary or tertiary alkanols. (5 marks)
(a) 2-butanol
(b) 2-methyl-2-propanol
(c) 2-methyl-1-propanol
(d) 3-pentanol
(e) 3-methyl-1-butanol
What type of isomerism is likely to exist for a compound with molecular formula, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$?
Give the name and structure of the isomers of $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$. (5 marks)
Name and give the molecular formula of functional derivatives of alkanoic acids. (5 marks)
What classes of organic homologues are commonly required to produce an alkanoate?

Give the names of the organic reagents required for the formation of these alkanoates
(i) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$
(ii) $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (5 marks)

Classify the following as primary, secondary or tertiary alkanamine. (5 marks)
(a) Trimethylamine
(b) 2-Aminopropane
(c) Dimethylamine
(d) Dimethyl Phenylamine
(e) 3-Aminopentane
Give the molecular polysaccharides.
Name two (2) naturally occurring disaccharides and two (2) polysaccharides. (5 marks)
What is vulcanization?
Name the monomer of natural rubber and state two (2) other monomers that have been employed for the production of synthetic rubber. (5 marks)

Using equation to illustrate what is meant by the terms
(i) Saponification
(ii) Esterification
(iii) Ethanoylation
(iv) Decarboxylation
(v) Dehydration (10 marks)

Give the name of the possible organic product(s) of the following transformation (10 marks)
(i) Dehydration of 2-butanol
(ii) Hydration of ethyne
(iii) Hydrochlorination of propene
(iv) Hydroxylation of ethene
(v) Reduction of 2-chloropropane

Draw displayed (structural) formulae for the following compounds:
(i) butanoyl chloride
(ii) ethanoic butanoic anhydride
(iii) ethyl 2-hydroxypropanoate
(iv) N-methyl, N-ethyl, 2-aminobutane
(v) sodium 2-hydroxyethanoate (5 marks)

Give the structure of product of the oxidation of these compounds. (6 marks)
(i) 1-Propanol
(ii) 2-propanol
(iii) 2-butanol

Give the structure of the product of the Clemmensen's reduction of these compounds. (4 marks)
(i) propanal
(ii) propanone
Calculate the molecular formula of an organic compound with $59.95\%$ carbon, $13.42\%$ hydrogen and $26.63\%$ oxygen; and whose vapour density is 30. (5 marks)
List five (5) primary uses of fats and oils. (5 marks)

Draw the repeating unit of the polymer formed by the reaction between butanedioic acid and hexane-1,6-diamine. State the type of polymerisation occurring in this reaction and give a name for the linkage between the monomer units in this polymer. (5 marks)

Give the reagent(s) required to convert ethanoyl chloride to the following compounds. (10 marks)
(i) $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$
(ii) $\text{CH}_3\text{COOC}_6\text{H}_5$
(iii) $\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2$
(iv) $\text{CH}_3\text{COC}_6\text{H}_5$
(v) $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-O-OC-CH}_3$

Indicate the structure of the compounds indicated by the symbols X and Y in this equation. (4 marks)
$$\text{H}_3\text{C-COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{Cl}_2 + \text{P / sunlight}} X \xrightarrow{\text{excess NH}_3} Y$$

Indicate the structure of the compounds indicated by the symbols X, Y and Z in these equations. (6 marks)
$$\text{H}_3\text{C-CHO} + \text{CH}_3\text{MgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} X$$
$$\text{H}_3\text{C-COCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{MgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} Y$$
$$\text{H}_3\text{C-C}\equiv\text{N} + \text{CH}_3\text{MgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} Z$$

The amino acid R is shown below:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\overset{\overset{\text{NH}_2}{\vert}}{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{COOH}$$
$$\text{R}$$
(i) Draw the structure of the zwitterion formed by R.
(ii) Draw the structure of the major organic product formed when an excess of R is reacted with bromomethane.
(iii) Name the mechanism of the reaction which results in the formation of the product given in part (ii). (5 marks)

There are several non-cyclic structural isomers with the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$. One of these isomers, 2-methylpent-2-ene, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, reacts with hydrogen bromide. Name the major product and account for its formation by reference to the mechanism of the reaction.

Identify one linear alkene of formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$ which can exist as a pair of stereoisomers. State the type of stereoisomerism shown, name the alkene and draw the structures of the two isomers. (11 marks)

Chloromethane can react with ammonia to produce a primary amine.
(i) What feature of the chloromethane molecule makes it susceptible to attack by an ammonia molecule?
(ii) Name the amine produced in this reaction.
(iii) Outline a mechanism for this reaction. (6 marks)

Ethene and other important hydrocarbons can be produced industrially from decane, $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{22}$. Name the process involved. Write two equations for reactions in which ethene is formed from decane by this process. Explain the economic importance of the process. (8 marks)
